Gemini Summary

Signal Summary:

  • Configuration statement: Given an inflation_signal z-score of 0.007863 and an inflation_signal_0_100 level of 20.48, this setup aligns with Downward-biased price paths and Indeterminate volatility, where the dominant risk is a Regime shift, not mean reversion (1).
  • The signal has entered a COOL regime as of May 2026, suggesting an abrupt shift from the previous Neutral state (1).
  • Conviction Band: Low; Interpretation Confidence: Low Confidence; Internal Conflict Flag: Yes. Signal Stability Assessment: Volatile; Threshold Proximity: Near; Revision Sensitivity: Unknown.

Methodology Applied:

  • COOL regime (<= -0.50) indicates disinflationary or deflationary pressure relative to the 10-year trend (1).
  • TRANSITION range (-0.25 to +0.25) signifies turning points or directionless inflationary environments (1).
  • Falling values imply disinflation, demand slowdown, or the effects of monetary tightening (1).
  • US Inflation Signal: latest observation 2026-05-31 (1).

Key Dynamics:

  • The primary driver is the sharp contraction in the composite z-score from 0.581 to 0.0078 within one month (1).
  • This represents a rapid negative momentum shift toward disinflationary territory (1).
  • Internal Conflict: The current z-score (0.0078) resides in the TRANSITION band, yet the data classifies it as COOL (1).
  • Conditional Invalidation: A move in the composite z-score above +0.25 would return the signal to Neutral (1).
  • Stability is currently low following the breakdown of the persistent Neutral regime held since late 2023 (1).

Scenario Balance:

  • Base case dominant: Persistent COOL regime supported by demand deceleration.
  • Upside risk: Mean reversion to Neutral triggered by a recovery in copper prices or M2 growth (1).
  • Downside risk: Deepening COOL regime (z-score < -0.50) triggered by significant industrial production contraction (1).

Time Horizon & Aggregation:

  • Time Horizon: Cyclical (months). Regimes are measured against a 10-year rolling window (1).
  • Aggregation Weight Hint: Low, due to the conflict between threshold definitions and current regime labeling (1).

Macro Relevance:

  • Informs aggregate latent inflation pressure across realized prices and monetary liquidity (1).
  • Economic mechanism: COOL suggests demand deceleration, which typically supports monetary easing and duration-heavy positions (1).
  • Cycle position: Not determined.
  • Interaction: Should be confirmed with liquidity (M2/Fed Assets) and USD strength (1).

Regime Context:

  • Newly entered COOL regime following a 26-month period of Neutral persistence (1).
  • Direction of change: Strengthening disinflationary impulse (1).

Model Limitations:

  • CPI is subject to revisions and base effects; TIPS liquidity can distort breakeven rates (1).
  • Revision window cannot be assessed from provided content.

Data & References:

  • US Inflation Signal: 2026-05-31 (1).
  • Most influential: Composite z-score (0.0078) and its rapid decline (1).
  • Additional public datasets: M2 Money Stock and 10Y Breakeven Inflation Rates would improve reliability.
